facts.raw_span: A 45-year-old African man presented with symptoms of palpitations, fatiguability, bipedal edema, weight loss, and diarrhea in the preceding weeks
He was a smoker with a 10 pack-year history
Blood pressure 136/87 mm Hg (MAP 103 mm Hg)
Fast atrial fibrillation with ventricular rates of 170 beats/min
S1 with loud, palpable P2, pansystolic murmurs in tricuspid and mitral areas

concepts.preferred_label: Atrial Fibrillation with Rheumatic Heart Disease
support_spans: Fast atrial fibrillation with ventricular rates of 170 beats/min
S1 with loud, palpable P2, pansystolic murmurs in tricuspid and mitral areas
concepts.why: The patient's atrial fibrillation and pansystolic murmurs are unusual and point to rheumatic heart disease.
The patient's bilateral lower-lobe acute pulmonary emboli are unusual and point to pulmonary embolism.
The patient's low left ventricular ejection fraction is unusual and points to cardiomyopathy.
The patient's hyperthyroidism and cardiac involvement are unusual and point to hyperthyroidism with cardiac involvement.
The patient's low thyroid-stimulating hormone and high free T4 levels suggest thyrotoxicosis, which can lead to thyroid storm.

support_spans: Fast atrial fibrillation with ventricular rates of 170 beats/min
concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of palpitations, fatiguability, and bipedal edema, along with the low left ventricular ejection fraction, suggest heart failure.
The CT pulmonary angiogram showing bilateral lower-lobe acute pulmonary emboli confirms the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism.

support_spans: Fast atrial fibrillation with ventricular rates of 170 beats/min
concepts.why: The patient's electrocardiogram showing rapid atrial fibrillation confirms the diagnosis of atrial fibrillation.
The patient's low thyroid-stimulating hormone and high free T4 levels suggest a hyperthyroid state, which can lead to atrial fibrillation and other cardiovascular symptoms.
The presence of bilateral lower-lobe acute pulmonary emboli on the CT Pulmonary Angiogram is a clear indication of pulmonary embolism.

support_spans: S1 with loud, palpable P2, pansystolic murmurs in tricuspid and mitral areas
concepts.why: The patient's cardiac auscultation findings, including a loud P2 and pansystolic murmurs in the mitral area, are consistent with mitral stenosis.

support_spans: Fast atrial fibrillation with ventricular rates of 170 beats/min
concepts.why: The patient's electrocardiogram shows rapid atrial fibrillation, which can lead to symptoms such as palpitations and fatigue.
